questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The doctor advised him to avoid eating sweets and doing exercise regularly.
o: avoiding sweets and doing regular exercise
to avoid sweets and to exercises regularly
to avoid eating sweets and to exercise regularly
to not eat sweets and do exercises
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'to avoid eating sweets and to exercise regularly'.
Key Points
  • The sentence discusses two pieces of advice given by the doctor: avoiding eating sweets and doing exercise regularly.
  • The correct form of the sentence must maintain parallelism in the construction of the two actions.
  • Option 3: "to avoid eating sweets and to exercise regularly" is the most appropriate option as it maintains grammatical correctness and parallel structure.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
Complete Sentence: "The doctor advised him to avoid eating sweets and to exercise regularly."
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "avoiding sweets and doing regular exercise" is incorrect because it uses "avoiding" instead of "to avoid," breaking the parallel structure.
  • Option 2: "to avoid sweets and to exercises regularly" is incorrect as "to exercises" is grammatically wrong (the correct form is "to exercise").
  • Option 4: "to not eat sweets and do exercises" is incorrect as it does not maintain proper parallel structure and uses "do exercises" instead of "to exercise."

questions.q: In an election, a voter has choices to vote for one candidate out of three candidates. There is also an option 'None Of The Above' (NOTA). The three candidates get votes that are $6$ times NOTA. The winner gets votes that are twice the second runner-up's votes. The first runner-up gets $900$ votes more than NOTA and defeats the second runner-up by $150$ votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.s: Dekh bhai, equations set karni hain. Total Cand = 6(NOTA). First RU = NOTA + 900. Second RU = First RU - 150 = NOTA + 750. Winner = 2(Second RU) = 2(NOTA) + 1500. Teeno candidates ka sum kar: $3(NOTA) + 900 + NOTA + 750 = 4(NOTA) + 3150$. Ye sum 6(NOTA) ke barabar hai. Toh $2(NOTA) = 3150 \implies NOTA = 1575$. Total votes = 7(NOTA) = $7 \times 1575 = 11025$.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs?
o: Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution;Fundamental Rights are optional
questions.s:
The Correct answer is Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not.

Key Points

  • Fundamental Rights are explicitly mentioned in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
  • They are enforceable by the courts, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated. This makes them justiciable.
  • The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs), enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution, are not enforceable by the courts, making them non-justiciable.
  • DPSPs act as guidelines for the government to achieve socio-economic goals and establish a welfare state.
  • While Fundamental Rights focus on individual rights and liberties, DPSPs emphasize collective welfare and societal development.
  • The Supreme Court of India has clarified that Fundamental Rights and DPSPs must be harmonized and not seen as conflicting entities.
  • Examples of Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality (Article 14-18) and the Right to Freedom (Article 19-22).
  • Examples of DPSPs include the directive to promote equal justice and free legal aid (Article 39A) and to ensure living wages for workers (Article 43).

Additional Information

  • Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
    • This option is incorrect because only Fundamental Rights are enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are not.
    • DPSPs serve as principles for governance and cannot be legally upheld in courts.
  • DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
    • The Supreme Court has ruled that Fundamental Rights hold a higher position in cases of conflict.
    • However, efforts have been made to harmonize both, recognizing their complementary nature.
  • DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional
    • This is incorrect as both Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are integral parts of the Constitution.
    • Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and enforceable, while DPSPs are guidelines that cannot be enforced legally.

questions.q: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of $x^2-8x+15$ and $x^2-5x+6$?
questions.s:
Answer is (x-2)(x-3)(x-5).
Dekh bhai... Dono quadratics ko factorize kar. Pehla: $x^2-8x+15 = (x-3)(x-5)$. Doosra: $x^2-5x+6 = (x-2)(x-3)$. LCM lene ke liye saare unique factors likh lo, jo common ho use ek baar likho. Toh highest superset ban gaya $(x-2)(x-3)(x-5)$. Simple school level algebra.

questions.q: A typist uses a paper of size 32 cm x 20 cm. He leaves a margin of 2cm each on all the sides. If he leaves a margin of 1 cm only on all the sides then what is the percentage of the increase in the area available for typing [correct to 2 decimal places]?
o:
20.54%

    79.46%
20.54%

questions.s:
Solution
If he leaves 2cm each
Length = 32 – 2 – 2 = 28
Breadth = 20 – 2 – 2 = 16
Area =28×16=448
If he leaves margin of 1cm each
Length = 32 – 1 – 1 = 30
Breadth = 20 – 1 – 1 = 18
Area =30×18=540
% change = ×100=20.54%

questions.q: Which of the following most accurately describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?
o: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.
questions.s:
The Correct answer is It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.

Key Points

  • Under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution, the right to property is no longer a fundamental right. It was demoted to a constitutional legal right by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
  • This article states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
  • This ensures that property can only be taken by the state through a legally established process, providing protection against arbitrary deprivation.
  • As a constitutional legal right, this provision primarily ensures that property rights are safeguarded as long as the deprivation occurs through proper legislation.
  • Unlike fundamental rights, violations of Article 300A cannot be directly challenged under Article 32 in the Supreme Court.
  • However, if property is taken away without following the due process of law, remedies can be sought through the High Courts under Article 226 or other legal avenues.
  • The transformation of the right to property from fundamental to constitutional legal right reflects the state's ability to regulate property for public welfare, subject to legal procedures.

Additional Information

  • It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
    • Before the 44th Amendment Act, the right to property was a fundamental right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31. However, post-amendment, Article 300A does not guarantee compensation for all acquisitions, and the right to property is now a constitutional legal right.
  • It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
    • This statement is incorrect as Article 300A explicitly requires deprivation to occur through the authority of law. Arbitrary deprivation without legal procedures violates the article.
  • It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.
    • Property rights under Article 300A cannot be enforced through Article 32, as they are not fundamental rights. Remedies for violations must be sought through High Courts under Article 226 or other legal mechanisms.

questions_hin.q_hi: What is the least common multiple (LCM) of $x^2-8x+15$ and $x^2-5x+6$?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Answer is (x-2)(x-3)(x-5).
Dekh bhai... Dono quadratics ko factorize kar. Pehla: $x^2-8x+15 = (x-3)(x-5)$. Doosra: $x^2-5x+6 = (x-2)(x-3)$. LCM lene ke liye saare unique factors likh lo, jo common ho use ek baar likho. Toh highest superset ban gaya $(x-2)(x-3)(x-5)$. Simple school level algebra.

questions_hin.q_hi: A typist uses a paper of size 32 cm x 20 cm. He leaves a margin of 2cm each on all the sides. If he leaves a margin of 1 cm only on all the sides then what is the percentage of the increase in the area available for typing [correct to 2 decimal places]?
o_hi:
20.54%

    82.96%

    17.04%    

    79.46%
20.54%
20.54%
questions_hin.s_hi:
Solution
If he leaves 2cm each
Length = 32 – 2 – 2 = 28
Breadth = 20 – 2 – 2 = 16
Area =28×16=448
If he leaves margin of 1cm each
Length = 32 – 1 – 1 = 30
Breadth = 20 – 1 – 1 = 18
Area =30×18=540
% change = ×100=20.54%

questions_hin.q_hi: Which of the following most accurately describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?
o_hi: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.
questions_hin.s_hi:
The Correct answer is It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.

Key Points

  • Under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution, the right to property is no longer a fundamental right. It was demoted to a constitutional legal right by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
  • This article states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
  • This ensures that property can only be taken by the state through a legally established process, providing protection against arbitrary deprivation.
  • As a constitutional legal right, this provision primarily ensures that property rights are safeguarded as long as the deprivation occurs through proper legislation.
  • Unlike fundamental rights, violations of Article 300A cannot be directly challenged under Article 32 in the Supreme Court.
  • However, if property is taken away without following the due process of law, remedies can be sought through the High Courts under Article 226 or other legal avenues.
  • The transformation of the right to property from fundamental to constitutional legal right reflects the state's ability to regulate property for public welfare, subject to legal procedures.

Additional Information

  • It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
    • Before the 44th Amendment Act, the right to property was a fundamental right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31. However, post-amendment, Article 300A does not guarantee compensation for all acquisitions, and the right to property is now a constitutional legal right.
  • It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
    • This statement is incorrect as Article 300A explicitly requires deprivation to occur through the authority of law. Arbitrary deprivation without legal procedures violates the article.
  • It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.
    • Property rights under Article 300A cannot be enforced through Article 32, as they are not fundamental rights. Remedies for violations must be sought through High Courts under Article 226 or other legal mechanisms.

questions_hin.q_hi: A reduction of $15\%$ in the price of wheat enables a housewife to buy $6$ kg more for $Rs$ $2720$. The reduced price per kg of wheat is?
questions_hin.s_hi: Dekh bhai, iska direct approach hai. $2720$ ka $15\%$ bach gaya price kam hone se. Kitna bacha? $2720 \times 0.15 = 408$. Is $408$ bache hue rupay me wo extra 6 kg le aayi. Toh naya (reduced) rate = $\frac{408}{6} = 68$ Rs/kg. Pen kam chala, dimaag zyada!
